problem.nature: Social Engineering - Phishing via Cloud Collaboration Tools

example.scenario: Phishing email with embedded malicious link to a fake cloud collaboration document, leading to malware download via shared Google Drive link with obfuscated URL parameters.

example.detection_method: Email gateway filters detect SPF fail and suspicious sender domain; URL scanning tools flag redirect parameter pointing to known malicious domain; Cloud DLP and CASB monitor external sharing event with suspicious domain; Endpoint AV detects Emotet payload hash during download; Network IDS alerts on HTTP requests with redirect parameter to evil-site.com; User training flags unexpected cloud share link.

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the stated problem of phishing via cloud collaboration tools. It includes a phishing email embedding a malicious link to a cloud-hosted document (Google Drive) with obfuscated URL parameters redirecting to a malware payload, which aligns well with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including email headers showing SPF failure, detailed SMTP logs, the malicious URL with redirect parameters, domain registration info indicating a suspicious domain, cloud action logs showing external sharing and file download, malware scan results confirming infection, and network capture data supporting the scenario. Indicators clearly highlight the malicious sender, domains, URL patterns, file hashes, IP addresses, and suspicious cloud events, effectively linking the sample to the problem description. The detection methods and relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are appropriate and well-mapped. All required fields are present and accurately populated, providing a complete and plausible real-world example. No issues were found.
